name: Botulinum Toxin
summary: A doctor-administered prescription injectable used to relax targeted muscles or reduce sweat-gland activity.
leadAnswer: Botulinum toxin is a prescription injectable that temporarily reduces the signal between nerves and the muscle or sweat gland it acts on. In aesthetic medicine it is used for expression lines, jaw and calf muscle bulk, and excessive sweating. It is a medicine, so a doctor must assess suitability before it can be prescribed or given.
suitableFor: Adults in general good health seeking assessment for dynamic expression lines
People bothered by excessive underarm, palm or sole sweating that has not responded to antiperspirants
People interested in assessment for jaw or calf muscle bulk
notSuitableFor: Known neuromuscular conditions such as myasthenia gravis or Lambert-Eaton syndrome
Known allergy to botulinum toxin or any component of the preparation
Active skin infection or inflammation at the intended injection site
Certain medications, including some antibiotics and muscle relaxants: bring a full list

comparisons.name: Botulinum toxin
comparisons.bestFor: Lines caused by muscle movement; sweating; muscle bulk

comparisons.name: Dermal fillers
comparisons.bestFor: Lines and hollows caused by lost volume or structure

preCare: Tell your doctor about all medicines and supplements, especially blood thinners, and any neuromuscular condition
Avoid alcohol for around 24 hours beforehand to reduce bruising
Come with the treatment area clean and free of make-up where possible
Reschedule if you have an active infection, rash or cold sore in the area
postCare: Stay upright for about four hours and avoid pressing, rubbing or massaging the area
Skip strenuous exercise, saunas, steam and hot yoga for the rest of the day
Avoid facials, facial massage and lying face-down for around 24 hours
Small raised bumps at the injection points usually settle within an hour
Contact the clinic if you notice drooping, double vision, swallowing or breathing difficulty

sections.heading: What is botulinum toxin?
body: Botulinum toxin is a purified protein produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum. In very small, controlled doses it is used in medicine to temporarily reduce the activity of a specific muscle or gland.
In Malaysia it is a prescription medicine: only a registered doctor can supply and administer it, after an in-person assessment.

sections.heading: How does botulinum toxin relax a muscle or sweat gland?
body: Muscles contract when a nerve releases a chemical messenger called acetylcholine at the junction between the nerve and the muscle. Botulinum toxin temporarily blocks that release, so the treated muscle contracts less strongly. The same mechanism applies to the nerves that switch on sweat glands, which is why it is also used for excessive sweating.
The effect is confined to the small area injected and is temporary: nerve signalling gradually returns and the muscle or gland resumes its usual activity, at a pace that varies between people.

sections.heading: What happens at a botulinum toxin appointment?
body: It starts with a consultation. The doctor watches the area at rest and in movement, explains what is and is not achievable, and goes through the risks. Only then is a dose decided.

The area is cleansed and the doctor gives a series of small injections with a fine needle at planned points. Most people describe brief stinging, and numbing or cooling can be used. Any change develops over the following days, and a review appointment checks it before anything further is decided.

sections.heading: What are the side effects of botulinum toxin?
body: Commonly reported temporary effects include tenderness, redness or small bruises at the injection points, and headache. These are usually mild and short-lived.

Less commonly, the effect extends slightly beyond the intended muscle, causing temporary asymmetry, a heavy-feeling brow or eyelid drooping, which can take weeks to resolve. Rarely, spread of the toxin has been reported to cause difficulty swallowing, speaking or breathing, or weakness away from the injection site. These need urgent medical attention.

sections.heading: How often is botulinum toxin repeated, and what affects the cost?
body: Because the effect wears off, treatment is a repeating cycle, not a course with an endpoint. How often depends on the area, the dose and how you respond, and is decided at review.
Cost depends on the area and the dose. As a prescription medicine it cannot be quoted or sold as a package before assessment.

faqs.a: No. Treatment is a repeating cycle, timed at review rather than on a fixed schedule.

faqs.q: Can it help with excessive sweating?
faqs.a: It is one option for excessive sweating of the underarms, palms or soles, usually where antiperspirants have not been enough. Underlying causes of the sweating are ruled out first.

faqs.q: Will my face look frozen or expressionless?
faqs.a: That look comes from dose and placement, which is why the doctor watches how your muscles move first. Say how much movement you want to keep.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Botox?
faqs.a: Botox is one registered brand of botulinum toxin type A: a product, not a separate treatment. Several brands are registered in Malaysia and differ in formulation and unit potency.

faqs.q: Is it the same as dermal filler?
faqs.a: No. Botulinum toxin relaxes muscle activity, so it addresses lines caused by movement. Dermal fillers add volume or structure, for hollowing and lines caused by lost volume. The two are sometimes used together.
